unit.why: The division holds two separate anecdotes about R. Heschel of Cracow, a pre-Hasidic rabbinic figure: R. Mordechai the rebuker who saw the Tosafists accompany him, and the Av Beit Din who failed to honour him and was corrected in a dream.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי שהיה מעשה כשהיה רבי ר' העשיל
stories.end_quote: בדבריהם קודם התפלה ומשום זה אחרתי לתפלה,
stories.summary_en: During a late village feast, the melamed R. Mordechai of Ratne rebukes R. Heschel of Cracow, who takes him to Cracow as his personal rebuker; later R. Mordechai resigns, explaining that the Tosafist R. Judah of Orleans accompanies Heschel to the study hall.

tags.why: praises R. Heschel of Cracow, a pre-Hasidic rabbinic authority

quotes: היה מלמד אחד שהיה נקרא שמו ר׳ מרדכי מראטנע

stories.start_quote: ופעם הלך הר״ר העשיל ליוינח והאב"ד
stories.end_quote: כי אם שאמרו לו מן השמים :
stories.summary_en: An Av Beit Din who slighted R. Heschel cannot explain a Tosafot passage Heschel asks him about; after he weeps, his late father appears in a dream, explains it, and warns him that Heschel holds the soul of Rabbenu Tam.

tags.why: praise of R. Heschel of Cracow, a pre-Hasidic figure

quotes: עד שבא אליו אביו בחלום ואמר לו פי׳ התוס׳
tags.why: a revelatory dream drives the plot

quotes: עד שבא אליו אביו בחלום
tags.why: the dead father speaks to his son

quotes: כי הוא נשמת ר"ת
tags.why: Heschel has the soul of Rabbenu Tam
